sentences.text: M/s. Joyguru Bhandar & Anr -vs-  The State of West Bengal & Ors

Mr. Phiroz Edulji,
 Mr. S. Lahiri, ... for the petitioners

Mr. Goutam Dinda,
 Mr. A.S. Chatterjee, ... for the O.P. No. 2.
Mrs. Purnima Ghosh,
... for the State.

The petitioners were convicted by the learned Magistrate, 2nd Court, Calcutta in Case No. 12D of 1996 under Sections 16(1) (a) (I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and petitioner No. 1 was sentenced to pay a fine of Rs 1,000/- and petitioner no. 2 was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a period of six months and also to pay fine of Rs. 1,000/-.

The judgment and order of conviction were affirmed on 22nd December, 2001 by learned the Learned 3rd Bench, City Sessions Court,
Calcutta in Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 1998.

Convict petitioners preferred an Appeal being C.R.R.
No. 54 of 2002 challenging the judgment and order passed in Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 1998.
On 9th June 2016 that revisional application was dismissed for default.

On 2nd April 2019 the petitioner prayed for restoration of the said revisional application by filing a separate application along with a prayer for condonation of delay in filing the application for restoration.
Re: CRAN 1472 of 2019 CRAN 1472 of 2019 is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
Petitioners have filed affidavit-of-service.
Learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 2 does not oppose the prayer for condonation of delay in filing the application for restoration of the main application.
Learned advocate appearing for the State leaves the matter to the discretion of the Court.
I think the main application requires to be disposed of on merit.

It has been contended by the petitioners that the petitioner No. 2 is a heart patient and he used to look after the case and due to his illness he could not look after the case properly and as a result the criminal revisional application was dismissed for default.
Considering all, the prayer for condonation of delay in filing the application is allowed.

sentences.text: Re : CRAN 1711 of 2018 CRAN 1711 of 2018 is taken up for hearing.
Heard the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the sides.
It appears that petitioner was prevented from sufficient cause to appear before the Court when the matter was called on for hearing.
Having regard to the submissions of the parties, I think it is a fit case to exercise the discretion in favour of the petitioners.
Let the Criminal revisional application be restored to its original file and number.
The restoration application being CRAN 1711 of 2018 is allowed.
Re: CRR 54 of 2002 It appears that the matter is pending for a long time.
Learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the Lower Court Records has been sent back to the learned Court below.
The Criminal Section is directed to take steps within two weeks from the date of deposit of the cost of Special Messenger by the petitioner.
Let the main application appear in the list on 16th July, 2019 for hearing as Contested Application.
( Madhumati Mitra, J. )
